content: To become a member of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), each prospective member is required to complete and submit a Declaration of Interests (DOI) form and provide a detailed curriculum vitae (CV). Additionally, a targeted and concise internet search is conducted to identify any apparent public controversies or interests that could potentially create compromising situations for the World Health Organization (WHO) or the expert in question. The steering committee members carefully review the candidate’s CV, DOI, and any information retrieved from the internet to assess whether there are, or could be, conflicts of interest (COI). If conflicts are identified, they determine whether these require a management plan. The management of COI is guided by WHO’s established protocols for DOI for experts, which include one-on-one consultations with a member of the Ethics Team from the WHO Office of Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics, as well as adherence to the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development. Both financial and non-financial interests are taken into account during this process. A “significant” conflict of interest may include the following scenarios: Intellectual bias: This occurs when an individual has repeatedly taken a public stance on an issue under review, potentially compromising their objectivity and independence in the global policy development process. Involvement in research or publication: This refers to participation in research activities or the publication of materials related to the issue under review. Financial interests exceeding USD $5,000: Any financial stake above this threshold is considered significant. For clear and ethical reasons, individuals who have been involved in the development of any assay are strictly excluded from participating in the policy development process. The WHO provides specific forms for the submission of DOI for experts, as outlined in the 2019 document titled Declaration of Interests for WHO Experts, which is accessible online. Additionally, the WHO Handbook for Guideline Development serves as a reference for these procedures.
